[USER] The user is planning to add new herbs to their garden, specifically mint and lemongrass.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is trying to create a garden that attracts bees and butterflies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is the practice of growing different plants together to improve their growth, health, and productivity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting can deter pests and diseases, attract beneficial insects, improve soil health, increase crop yields, and enhance flavor and nutrition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant asked what type of plants the user is planning to add to their garden and if they are looking to grow vegetables, fruits, herbs, or flowers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant acknowledged the user's attendance at a gardening workshop and noted that community gardens and workshops are excellent resources for learning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mint and lemongrass are great additions to a pollinator-friendly garden and will attract bees and butterflies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested companion planting for mint includes bee-friendly companions like lavender, coneflower, and black-eyed Susan, as well as pest-repelling companions like tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested companion planting for lemongrass includes pollinator-friendly companions like marigold, zinnia, and cosmos, as well as pest-repelling companions like citronella grass or basil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested general tips for creating a pollinator-friendly garden include planting a variety of flowers that bloom at different times, incorporating native plants, avoiding pesticides, and providing a source of water.  
[USER] The user is thinking of adding marigolds to their garden.  
[USER] The user learned at the workshop that marigolds can help deter nematodes, which can harm tomatoes.  
[USER] The user asked if adding marigolds is a good idea.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marigolds are an excellent addition to the garden, especially for tomatoes, as they are a natural nematode repellent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marigolds contain a chemical called alpha-terthienyl, which is toxic to nematodes and can help reduce their population in the soil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Benefits of planting marigolds with tomatoes include nematode control, pest control, soil health improvement, and companion planting.
